notes: ACCESS: https://www.myer.com.au/robots.txt fetched FIRST via probe.fetch (HTTP 200, safari18_0_ios, 994 bytes). NO Claude / ClaudeBot / anthropic-ai / Claude-Web group - a single `User-agent: *` group plus two Sitemap lines. Myer did NOT present a bot wall to probe.fetch: every page returned HTTP 200 first or second fingerprint, so no campaign-parameter fetch, no reader and no browser was needed or used (BATCH_BRIEF s2 ladder not required). ROBOTS COMPLIANCE IN DETAIL, because this file is restrictive: `Disallow: /*facets=` (allowed only under /buy/) - I never requested a facets URL; `Disallow: /*sort=` - I never sent a sort parameter; `Disallow: */search*` - I never used internal search; `Disallow: /*/all$` - none of my URLs ends in /all (note /c/home/allbathroom is a single segment 'allbathroom', not '/all'); `Disallow: /*pageNumber*pageNumber*` forbids only a DOUBLED pageNumber, so the single `?pageNumber=N` form I used for enumeration is permitted; `Disallow: /women/ /men/ /beauty/ /kidsbaby/ /electrical/ /gifts/ /offers/ /promo/ /webapp/*` are root-level paths and Myer's category URLs are /c/<dept>/..., but I stayed inside /c/home/ and /c/home/all-furniture/ anyway and requested none of those departments. PER-HOST: everything is served from www.myer.com.au - the PLPs are server-rendered Next.js pages that ship their own Fredhopper category payload inline, so no separate API host was contacted; the two sitemap files are on the same host. TREE: taken from the site's OWN catalogue payload, not guessed. Every Myer page embeds __NEXT_DATA__.props.pageProps.dehydratedState.queries, and the ['catalogue'] query carries the COMPLETE 815KB category tree for all 11 top departments (New In, Women, Men, Beauty, Home, Travel & Tech, Kids, Toys, Gifts, Sale, MYER one) with name / categoryId / seoToken / description for every node. The full Bathroom footprint, recovered from that tree and cross-checked against the ['category'] query on each page: Home > Bathroom (s_home_bathroom, seo allbathroom, id 457614, 1126) with children Bath Towels (544), Bath Mats (71), Bathrobes (66), Bathroom Accessories (418) and a cross-listed Cleaning node (27); Bathroom Accessories has five children - Bathroom Organisation (246), Toilet Brushes & Sets (27), Soap Dispensers (30), Bathroom Scales (29), Bathroom Mirrors (43); and a SECOND branch under Home > Furniture: Bathroom Furniture (83) with Bathroom Cabinets & Vanities (16) and Bathroom Fittings (52), plus Home > Furniture > Home Storage > Bathroom & Laundry Storage (87). I did not stop at the mega-menu: I regex-swept the ENTIRE catalogue tree (all departments) for bath|shower|toilet|soap|towel|vanit|basin|sanitar|bidet|faucet|washroom|mirror|toothbrush and inspected every hit. Everything else is out of scope - Beauty > Bath & Body and every brand's Bath & Body (cosmetics), Kids > Nursery > Bath & Change (baby bathing, toiletries, bath toys, potties), Men/Travel > Toiletry Bags (luggage), Home > Kitchen > Kitchen Linen > Tea Towels, Home > Outdoor > Beach & Pool > Beach Towels, Home > Personal Care Appliances > Dental Care > Electric Toothbrushes (appliance, not a bathroom accessory), and the whole Sale/Clearance and New In mirror-trees (New In > Home > Bathroom, Sale > Home Sale > Bathroom and its four children, Sale > Clearance > Home Clearance > Bathroom, Sale > ... > Bathroom Furniture, Sale > ... > Bathroom & Laundry Storage) which are promotional re-cuts of the same nodes and are banned by rule 25 - recording any of them would duplicate the recorded leaves. QTY: source is `productTotalCount` in each page's own ['category', <path>, <page>, [], 'relevance'] payload - the exact field the PLP header and grid render from - and it was PROVED, not assumed. (a) Direct equivalence on small nodes, where Fredhopper sets productsPerPage == the total: Bathroom Mirrors 43 = perPage 43 = productList length 43; Bathroom Scales 29 = 29 = 29; Soap Dispensers 30 = 30 = 30; Toilet Brushes 27 = 27 = 27; Cleaning 27 = 27 = 27; Cabinets & Vanities 16 = 16 = 16. (b) EXHAUSTIVE UNIQUE-ID ENUMERATION via ?pageNumber=N on ten nodes of five different sizes, counting distinct product ids: Bathrobes 66 = 66 (48+18), Bathroom Fittings 52 = 52 (48+4), Bath Mats 71 = 71 (48+23), Bathroom & Laundry Storage 87 = 87 (48+39), Bathroom Organisation 246 = 246 (5x48 + 6), Bathroom Accessories 418 = 418, Bathroom Furniture 83 = 83, Home Decor Mirrors 225 = 225. Every page returned a DIFFERENT product set with the offset advancing correctly (0, 48, 96, ...) and zero duplicate ids across pages, so this is not the IKEA re-serve trap; and the last page's short length matches total mod 48 exactly in every case. (c) Roll-up consistency: the Bathroom department's five children sum to exactly 544+71+66+418+27 = 1126 = its own productTotalCount, an independent arithmetic confirmation. Counts discriminate strongly per node (1126/544/418/246/87/83/71/66/52/43/30/29/27/27/16) with no round-number cap and no site-wide constant, and each page's category.description matched the node requested. NO figure was estimated and none came from a facet, sort or search URL. DEDUP (OPTION 1): already_extracted() run on every candidate leaf, every review node and every parent. The index holds 73 myer.com.au URLs (32 Furniture.xlsx, 41 Final.xlsx). ONE bathroom hit: /c/home/all-furniture/furniture-bathroom/cabinets-vanities is in Furniture.xlsx as 'Bathroom Cabinets & Vanities' - it stays there and is in review, not rows. The four recorded Bathroom Accessories leaves, Bathroom Fittings, and the Bathroom/Bathroom Accessories/Bathroom Furniture parents are all ABSENT from the index. Critical near-miss checked and cleared: /c/home/furniture-home-decor/wall-art--1/home-decor-mirrors IS already extracted in Final.xlsx as 'Mirrors', so I enumerated both mirror nodes in full and proved the intersection of its 225 ids with Bathroom Mirrors' 43 ids is ZERO - the recorded Bathroom Mirrors node is a genuinely separate population, not a re-extraction. Blind spots: (a) canonical - each recorded URL is served under exactly one seoToken path built from the catalogue's own parent chain, no alias observed; (b)/(c) locale - myer.com.au is single-locale en-AU with no country subdomain or hreflang alternate, so no locale variant can hide an extracted node; (d) two nav paths - the Sale and New In trees re-expose the same categoryIds under different seoTokens and are excluded under rule 25 rather than recorded twice. ROUTING: bath towels (544), bath mats (71) and bathrobes (66) go to Textile; the Cleaning node goes nowhere (kitchen utility); Bathroom Scales and Bathroom & Laundry Storage are held in review at LOW confidence rather than guessed. RECORDED: 4 leaves under Bathroom Accessories (Organisation 246, Toilet Brushes & Sets 27, Soap Dispensers 30, Bathroom Mirrors 43) and 1 leaf under Bathroom Furniture (Fittings 52). Bathroom Fittings was inspected product-by-product and is the strongest find on the site under rules 6/8/14: Cefito and My Plaza basin, bath, shower and wall mixer taps and faucets in brass/chrome/black, wall spouts, shower mixer sets and Cefito non-electric and electric bidet toilet seats - rule 8 explicitly allows metallic taps.
